# Notes.ThatVetGuy

> Free academic resources, thoughtfully made for future vets.

A free academic library for BVSc & AH students. Site summaries: Dr. Chirag Patidar, BVSc & AH, MVSc. Notes, books and practical material are organised by professional year and subject. File links open on Google Drive. Known source credits are preserved; inclusion does not imply authorship or medical review.

Main website: https://thatvetguy.net
Author: Dr. Chirag Patidar
Last source review: 2026-10-14. File access settings can change.

---
Canonical: https://notes.thatvetguy.net/

# BVSc Notes & Books

Free notes, books and practical material for all four BVSc & AH professional years. Choose your year, then your subject.

[BVSc & AH1st year3 subjects · 453 resources](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/)[BVSc & AH2nd year5 subjects · 325 resources](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/)[BVSc & AH3rd year7 subjects · 549 resources](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/)[BVSc & AH4th year4 subjects · 371 resources](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/)

Year grouping may vary by university. Check your syllabus. Counts combine alternate formats and photo sets into single resources.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Anatomy focuses on relating structure to function across domestic animal species. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Use labelled diagrams to compare the same structure between species, then explain its functional significance.

- Osteology and arthrology
- Myology and visceral anatomy
- Neuroanatomy and sense organs
- Histology and embryology

Use labelled diagrams to compare the same structure between species, then explain its functional significance.

## Keep the connections.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Physiology focuses on understanding how healthy animals maintain normal body functions. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Draw a process from stimulus to response before learning the individual hormones, transporters or feedback loops.

- Blood and cardiovascular physiology
- Respiratory and renal physiology
- Digestion and metabolism
- Endocrine and reproductive physiology

Draw a process from stimulus to response before learning the individual hormones, transporters or feedback loops.

What to revise in this subject 

Livestock Production Management focuses on connecting animal husbandry principles with practical farm management. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare management requirements by species, age and production stage, with welfare and daily observation in view.

- Housing and animal handling
- Cattle and buffalo management
- Sheep and goat management
- Poultry production and farm records

Compare management requirements by species, age and production stage, with welfare and daily observation in view.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Biochemistry focuses on linking molecular processes with animal health and nutrition. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Build pathway maps around inputs, outputs and regulation instead of memorising disconnected reaction names.

- Carbohydrate, lipid and protein metabolism
- Enzymes and biological oxidation
- Vitamins and minerals
- Molecular biology and biochemical tests

Build pathway maps around inputs, outputs and regulation instead of memorising disconnected reaction names.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Microbiology focuses on distinguishing infectious agents and the host responses they provoke. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare each agent by classification, transmission and laboratory identification while keeping species context clear.

- Bacteriology and mycology
- Veterinary virology
- Immunology
- Microbial genetics and biotechnology

Compare each agent by classification, transmission and laboratory identification while keeping species context clear.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Pathology focuses on recognising mechanisms of disease and the lesions they produce. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Link the underlying mechanism to gross and microscopic changes, then practise describing lesions precisely.

- Cell injury and inflammation
- Circulatory disturbances
- Systemic pathology
- Necropsy and diagnostic sampling

Link the underlying mechanism to gross and microscopic changes, then practise describing lesions precisely.

What to revise in this subject 

Animal Genetics and Breeding focuses on applying inheritance and population principles to animal improvement. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Work through inheritance and selection examples step by step, checking assumptions before interpreting the result.

- Mendelian and molecular genetics
- Population and quantitative genetics
- Selection and breeding systems
- Animal breeding programmes

Work through inheritance and selection examples step by step, checking assumptions before interpreting the result.

What to revise in this subject 

Animal Nutrition focuses on understanding feeds, nutrient requirements and feeding systems. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare nutrient requirements with feed characteristics and production stage before attempting a balanced ration.

- Feed evaluation and digestion
- Energy and protein nutrition
- Minerals and vitamins
- Ration formulation and species feeding

Compare nutrient requirements with feed characteristics and production stage before attempting a balanced ration.

- Review practical observations alongside the related theory.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology focuses on connecting drug action with species, safety and clinical context. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Organise drug classes by mechanism, indications and adverse effects; verify clinical details against a current professional reference.

- General pharmacology and pharmacokinetics
- Systemic pharmacology
- Antimicrobial and antiparasitic agents
- Toxicology and poisoning principles

Organise drug classes by mechanism, indications and adverse effects; verify clinical details against a current professional reference.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Parasitology focuses on understanding parasite life cycles and their significance in animal health. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Sketch life cycles with hosts and infective stages, then connect those stages to diagnosis and prevention.

- Helminthology
- Veterinary protozoology
- Veterinary entomology and acarology
- Parasitological diagnosis and control

Sketch life cycles with hosts and infective stages, then connect those stages to diagnosis and prevention.

## Keep the connections.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Public Health and Epidemiology focuses on connecting animal health, human health and population evidence. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Separate individual clinical findings from population measures, and state the denominator whenever interpreting disease frequency.

- Zoonoses and One Health
- Food safety and hygiene
- Measures of disease frequency
- Disease investigation and prevention

Separate individual clinical findings from population measures, and state the denominator whenever interpreting disease frequency.

What to revise in this subject 

Livestock Products Technology focuses on following animal products from production through processing and safety. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Use process flow diagrams to connect preservation methods, product quality and the purpose of each processing step.

- Milk processing and dairy products
- Meat science and meat products
- Poultry and egg products
- By-products, quality and preservation

Use process flow diagrams to connect preservation methods, product quality and the purpose of each processing step.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary and Animal Husbandry Extension Education focuses on communicating animal husbandry knowledge in ways communities can use. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Match the communication method to the audience and explain how you would assess whether the advice was understood.

- Extension principles and teaching methods
- Rural sociology and communication
- Programme planning and evaluation
- Livestock entrepreneurship and advisory services

Match the communication method to the audience and explain how you would assess whether the advice was understood.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Medicine focuses on organising clinical reasoning around animal diseases and presenting problems. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Build problem lists before differential diagnoses, and compare diseases by distinguishing findings rather than isolated facts.

- General and systemic medicine
- Infectious and metabolic diseases
- Preventive medicine and herd health
- Diagnostic reasoning and case management

Build problem lists before differential diagnoses, and compare diseases by distinguishing findings rather than isolated facts.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Surgery and Radiology focuses on understanding surgical principles alongside diagnostic imaging. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Connect anatomy, patient preparation and procedural reasoning; clinical techniques require supervised training and current guidance.

- Asepsis and surgical principles
- Anaesthesiology and pain management
- Soft tissue surgery and orthopaedics
- Radiography and other imaging principles

Connect anatomy, patient preparation and procedural reasoning; clinical techniques require supervised training and current guidance.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Gynaecology and Obstetrics focuses on understanding reproduction, fertility and obstetrical principles across species. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare reproductive timelines by species, then relate abnormal findings to the relevant stage and clinical history.

- Reproductive cycles and breeding
- Infertility and reproductive disorders
- Pregnancy and parturition
- Obstetrics, andrology and assisted reproduction

Compare reproductive timelines by species, then relate abnormal findings to the relevant stage and clinical history.

What to revise in this subject 

Veterinary Clinical Practices II focuses on integrating supervised clinical learning across the final professional year. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Present cases with a concise history, problem list and reasoned plan, and document what needs further confirmation.

- Clinical examination and diagnostic planning
- Medical and surgical case discussions
- Reproductive case assessment
- Hospital records and clinical communication

Present cases with a concise history, problem list and reasoned plan, and document what needs further confirmation.

4th Year Road Map 

- Organise Medicine, Surgery and Gynaecology notes by your syllabus topics.
- Connect each case discussion with the relevant subject notes and practical record.
- Use current clinical guidance and supervision; study notes are not prescribing advice.

Year grouping may vary by university. Check your syllabus.

Last checked: 2026-10-18. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

# Veterinary Anatomy

Veterinary Anatomy focuses on relating structure to function across domestic animal species. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Use labelled diagrams to compare the same structure between species, then explain its functional significance.

[Read Veterinary Anatomy resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-anatomy/)

## Your revision outline

- Osteology and arthrology
- Myology and visceral anatomy
- Neuroanatomy and sense organs
- Histology and embryology

Use labelled diagrams to compare the same structure between species, then explain its functional significance.

Last checked: 2026-10-18. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/[BVSc](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/)/Veterinary Physiology

# Veterinary Physiology

Veterinary Physiology focuses on understanding how healthy animals maintain normal body functions. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Draw a process from stimulus to response before learning the individual hormones, transporters or feedback loops.

[Read Veterinary Physiology resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-physiology/)

## Your revision outline

- Blood and cardiovascular physiology
- Respiratory and renal physiology
- Digestion and metabolism
- Endocrine and reproductive physiology

Draw a process from stimulus to response before learning the individual hormones, transporters or feedback loops.

Last checked: 2026-10-18. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

# Livestock Production Management

Livestock Production Management focuses on connecting animal husbandry principles with practical farm management. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare management requirements by species, age and production stage, with welfare and daily observation in view.

[Read Livestock Production Management resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/livestock-production-management/)

## Your revision outline

- Housing and animal handling
- Cattle and buffalo management
- Sheep and goat management
- Poultry production and farm records

Compare management requirements by species, age and production stage, with welfare and daily observation in view.

# Veterinary Biochemistry

Veterinary Biochemistry focuses on linking molecular processes with animal health and nutrition. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Build pathway maps around inputs, outputs and regulation instead of memorising disconnected reaction names.

[Read Veterinary Biochemistry resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-biochemistry/)

## Your revision outline

- Carbohydrate, lipid and protein metabolism
- Enzymes and biological oxidation
- Vitamins and minerals
- Molecular biology and biochemical tests

Build pathway maps around inputs, outputs and regulation instead of memorising disconnected reaction names.

Last checked: 2026-10-18. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

# Veterinary Microbiology

Veterinary Microbiology focuses on distinguishing infectious agents and the host responses they provoke. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare each agent by classification, transmission and laboratory identification while keeping species context clear.

[Read Veterinary Microbiology resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-microbiology/)

## Your revision outline

- Bacteriology and mycology
- Veterinary virology
- Immunology
- Microbial genetics and biotechnology

Compare each agent by classification, transmission and laboratory identification while keeping species context clear.

Last checked: 2026-10-18. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

# Veterinary Pathology

Veterinary Pathology focuses on recognising mechanisms of disease and the lesions they produce. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Link the underlying mechanism to gross and microscopic changes, then practise describing lesions precisely.

[Read Veterinary Pathology resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-pathology/)

## Your revision outline

- Cell injury and inflammation
- Circulatory disturbances
- Systemic pathology
- Necropsy and diagnostic sampling

Link the underlying mechanism to gross and microscopic changes, then practise describing lesions precisely.

Last checked: 2026-10-18. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

# Animal Genetics and Breeding

Animal Genetics and Breeding focuses on applying inheritance and population principles to animal improvement. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Work through inheritance and selection examples step by step, checking assumptions before interpreting the result.

[Read Animal Genetics and Breeding resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/)

## Your revision outline

- Mendelian and molecular genetics
- Population and quantitative genetics
- Selection and breeding systems
- Animal breeding programmes

Work through inheritance and selection examples step by step, checking assumptions before interpreting the result.

Last checked: 2026-10-18. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

# Animal Nutrition

Animal Nutrition focuses on understanding feeds, nutrient requirements and feeding systems. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Compare nutrient requirements with feed characteristics and production stage before attempting a balanced ration.

[Read Animal Nutrition resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-nutrition/)

## Your revision outline

- Feed evaluation and digestion
- Energy and protein nutrition
- Minerals and vitamins
- Ration formulation and species feeding

Compare nutrient requirements with feed characteristics and production stage before attempting a balanced ration.

# Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology

Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology focuses on connecting drug action with species, safety and clinical context. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Organise drug classes by mechanism, indications and adverse effects; verify clinical details against a current professional reference.

[Read Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-pharmacology-and-toxicology/)

## Your revision outline

- General pharmacology and pharmacokinetics
- Systemic pharmacology
- Antimicrobial and antiparasitic agents
- Toxicology and poisoning principles

Organise drug classes by mechanism, indications and adverse effects; verify clinical details against a current professional reference.

## Your revision outline

- Helminthology
- Veterinary protozoology
- Veterinary entomology and acarology
- Parasitological diagnosis and control

Sketch life cycles with hosts and infective stages, then connect those stages to diagnosis and prevention.

# Veterinary Public Health and Epidemiology

Veterinary Public Health and Epidemiology focuses on connecting animal health, human health and population evidence. This guide helps BVSc & AH students locate credited notes and year-wise book collections, with a short revision outline to organise reading. Separate individual clinical findings from population measures, and state the denominator whenever interpreting disease frequency.

[Read Veterinary Public Health and Epidemiology resources ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-public-health-and-epidemiology/)

## Your revision outline

- Zoonoses and One Health
- Food safety and hygiene
- Measures of disease frequency
- Disease investigation and prevention

Separate individual clinical findings from population measures, and state the denominator whenever interpreting disease frequency.

# Veterinary Medicine

Veterinary Medicine focuses on organising clinical reasoning around animal diseases and presenting problems. ## Your revision outline

- General and systemic medicine
- Infectious and metabolic diseases
- Preventive medicine and herd health
- Diagnostic reasoning and case management

# Clinical Resources

Veterinary handbooks and pharmacology notes for students preparing for clinical work. Start with a reference or explore Medicine, Surgery, Pathology and Pharmacology.

For study, not prescribing. Verify the species, dose and current clinical guidance before treating a patient.

↳ Check the dose. Then check it again. The patient can't.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/Tips & Tools for Vet Study

# Tips & Tools for Vet Study

Explore practical AI study guidance, useful free apps and everyday study tools for veterinary students. Use the guides to organise reading, references and presentations while checking veterinary information against trusted sources.

## Use of AI for Vet Study

↳ AI can help with the notes. You still have to read them.

- 

### Start with your outline

Ask AI to organise a topic list or suggest a presentation structure. Compare the result with your syllabus and original notes.

- 

### Check before you learn

Verify veterinary facts and citations. A fluent answer can still be wrong; AI output is not a prescribing reference.

- 

### Make the explanation yours

Explain the topic without looking at the answer. Rewrite it in your own words and credit your sources.

## Useful Free Apps

- 

### Zotero

Keep reading references together. Check each citation against its original source.

- 

### LibreOffice

Prepare notes, tables and presentations. Keep an editable copy as well as a PDF.

- 

### Your PDF reader

Use bookmarks, annotations and text search. Keep essential reading in a clearly named offline folder.

## Useful Study Tools

- 

### A document scanner

Scan only material you have permission to copy. Check every page for legibility before sharing.

- 

### A simple folder system

Try Year / Subject / Notes or Books. A useful filename saves a surprising amount of searching.

- 

### A reference checklist

Record the author, edition, species and date where relevant. A saved file still needs context.

## Charts & Tables

Study charts and statistical tables from the subject collections.

[PPTPedegree ChartLivestock Production Management · Slides](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/livestock-production-management/#file-1jqfABHLlw_gDbffe188k1-9QCcD2gK7f)
[DOCDistribution TablesAnimal Genetics and Breeding · Practical](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/#file-1F4VgJziYlOGh17x4D2o9c1J9Yj3oMK9N)
[PDFF-tableAnimal Genetics and Breeding · Note](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/#file-1tMqWIPLPxMiYJHIeHEHk62O6DLc2PD-L)
[PDFt (Student's) tableAnimal Genetics and Breeding · Note](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/#file-1eNJf0tPojv7FY3EQZXGtjl_g2VkIQlNs)

## Templates & Formats

Copy these simple outlines into your own document. Adapt practical records to your department’s required format.

### One-topic revision note

Topic · Definition · Key points · Labelled diagram · Common confusions · Source and page.

### Practical record outline

Date · Title · Aim · Materials · Method · Observations · Result · Precautions · Reference.

## Useful Links

Go straight to the part of the library you need.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/About Notes.ThatVetGuy

# About Notes.ThatVetGuy

Notes.ThatVetGuy is a free academic library for BVSc & AH students. Find notes, books and practical material by year, with study guides to help you choose what to read next.

## A useful place to start.

Pick your professional year, find a subject and get to the reading. Notes.ThatVetGuy brings notes, books and practical material together for veterinary students.

## People behind the pages

Site guidance and summaries are by Dr. Chirag Patidar, BVSc & AH, MVSc. Linked materials retain their original authorship. Inclusion does not imply medical review or ownership.

## Help the next student

A missing topic, a broken file or a credit that needs correcting: tell us so the library can get better.

[Request or report a resource ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/)

## Questions, answered

Where do files open?

Resources open on Google Drive. Photo batches appear as one set, alternate formats share a row, and exact duplicates are hidden. Original authors retain credit.

Does the year grouping match my syllabus?

Year grouping may vary by university. Check your syllabus before planning revision.

Last checked: 2026-10-18. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.

Canonical: https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/

<!-- Canonical: https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/; updated: 2026-10-18 -->

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/Can’t find what you need?

# Can’t find what you need?

Request a veterinary note, book, PYQ or useful study resource, or report a link that needs attention. Include the subject, year and source so the library can be improved for other veterinary students.

↳ Can't find it? Ask. The library has an excellent memory.

## Tell us what would help.

Include the topic, subject, year and edition if relevant.

File ID, if reporting a file

[Email your request ](mailto:contact@thatvetguy.net?subject=Resource%20request)

You can also copy contact@thatvetguy.net into your email app.

## Contact

Send your question to contact@thatvetguy.net.

## Contribute

Send the title, subject and original source credit. Share only material you have permission to contribute.

## Report an error / takedown

Include the file ID or page URL, the issue and your contact details. For a takedown request, explain your connection to the material.

## Questions, answered

How do I report a broken link?

Email contact@thatvetguy.net with the page URL and resource name. The visible email address can be copied if your email application does not open.

Can I contribute a resource?

Send the original source, title and subject to contact@thatvetguy.net. Share material you have permission to contribute.

Last checked: 2026-10-18. This date records source review, not a guarantee of external file availability.
